Niche Academy is a simple learning platform with easy to follow tutorials. Learn how to use anything from social media platforms to resources available from the North Liberty Library.

## North Liberty Digital History Collection

Search through North Liberty Historical records. Letters, photos, books, and more! Access is free and we invite you to contribute to the collection!

## ParentTV

ParentTV offers thousands of on-demand parenting videos and courses with content designed to support those who care for children, from pregnancy through to teenage years.

## The Gazette

While inside the North Liberty Community Center enjoy unlimited free access to thegazette.com. Made possible in partnership with The Gazette and your area public libraries.

## The New York Times

Enjoy free access to NYTimes.com courtesy of your libraries in Digital Johnson County. To activate your subscription, you’ll need to log in or register (with your email and password). Please note, you will need to re-redeem access every 72 hours.

## The Wall Street Journal

Get unlimited access to breaking business, financial and world news from The Wall Street Journal. To activate your subscription, you’ll need to log in or register (with your email and password). Please note, you will need to re-redeem access every 72 hours.

## The Washington Post

The Washington Post provides world-class coverage of the day’s most important local, national and international news.

## Unite for Literacy

Unite for Literacy provides engaging digital picture books complete with audio narration options in a variety of languages.

## Value Line

Value Line provides access to leading research publications covering stocks, mutual funds, options and convertible securities as well as our proprietary special situation stocks.

## World Book Online

A comprehensive suite of e-learning resources designed for all ages and abilities with articles, videos, educator tools, eBooks, research guides and more.

The North Liberty Library’s meeting and study spaces are available during operating hours on a first-come, first-served basis for individual, nonprofit, educational, civic, and informational gatherings that are open to the public. Use of the rooms does not imply endorsement by the Library or the City of North Liberty, and commercial sales and private parties are not permitted.

## Reservation Details

Choose your date, start time, end time (up to three hours), and group size, then select Search to view available spaces. Once you’ve selected a room, you’ll be prompted to enter your reservation details, including your name, phone number, and email.

- An individual or group may have up to four (3) reservations scheduled at a time.
- Meeting/study rooms may be reserved for a maximum of three (3) hours unless prearranged; extensions may be permitted upon request if space is available.

__data__.text:
## Help Set Our Direction

Volunteers, appointed by North Liberty’s Mayor and confirmed by the City Council, help advise on a wide range of areas, including land use and zoning, parks and recreation programs, and library policy.

Appointment to a volunteer board or commission means you can make a difference in many aspects of community development. Take this opportunity to volunteer your time to serve on any one of the following. Most terms begin on July 1 of each year, but openings sometimes occur during the year.

## Board & Commission Meetings

Board and commission meetings are open to the public and typically meet on a recurring cycle in the City Council Chambers at City HAll, 360 N. Main St. You can attend these meetings live in person, or watch them live online.

## Apply to Serve

Applications are available at City Hall, 360 N. Main Street or online. Completed applications can be submitted at City Hall or via email to \[email protected\]. Applicants must be 18 years old and a legal resident of the city.

Appointments are made by the Mayor with the City Council’s approval. Commissions that assist in department overview and making recommendations to City Council. Members are appointed by the mayor and approved by the city council.

## Boards, Committees & Commissions

## Board of Adjustment

A five-member board charged with approving variances and conditional uses for buildings in North Liberty. It meets as needed.

## Board of Appeals

A five-member board charged with hearing appeals regarding the application and interpretation of the North Liberty building code. It meets as needed.

**Anna Lenoch**

Through June 2027

**Joshua Scanlon**

Through June 2028

## Cemetery Board

A six-member board (three from North Liberty and three from Penn Township) charged with overseeing Ridgewood Cemetery on Scales Bend Road.
